excerpt: PayMongo is a BSP-regulated Philippine payment gateway for cards, GCash, Maya, QR Ph and online banking. Fees, founders, funding and alternatives.
content:
PayMongo is a payments company in the Philippines that lets businesses accept money online and in store. Through a single account, merchants can take Visa and Mastercard cards, e-wallets such as GCash, Maya, GrabPay and ShopeePay, QR Ph codes, direct online banking from banks like BDO, BPI and UnionBank, and buy-now-pay-later through BillEase. It offers an API and e-commerce plugins for developers, plus no-code payment links and pages, and adds payouts, a storefront product and fraud screening. Its about page says it is regulated by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, is based in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, and serves more than 350,000 businesses.

PayMongo was founded in May 2019. TechCrunch named its co-founders as Francis Plaza (CEO), Jaime Hing III (CTO) and Luis Sia (chief commercial officer). The company went through Y Combinator. Its $12 million Series A in 2020 was led by Stripe, and in February 2022 it raised a $31 million Series B with new investors including JAM Fund, ICCP-SBI Venture Partners and Kaya Founders, and returning backers Global Founders Capital and SOMA Capital, bringing total funding to just under $46 million. At the time it said it would add disbursements, lending, buy-now-pay-later and recurring payments, and explore expansion in Southeast Asia. Its about page also lists Founders Fund among its investors.

Fees are published. When we checked, there was no setup fee. QR Ph cost 1.34% per transaction, local cards 3.125% plus ₱13.39, international cards 4.02% plus ₱13.39, GCash 2.23%, Maya 1.79%, GrabPay 1.96%, ShopeePay 1.70%, and direct online banking 0.71% or ₱13.39, all before VAT. Payouts cost ₱10 each through InstaPay or PESONet, and the online storefront costs ₱349 a month.

This page is research, not a review. We have not processed payments with PayMongo; facts come from its pages and TechCrunch.
